title: The Guadalajara Mexico Temple is opened in Mexico City.
text: The Guadalajara Mexico Temple is a temple of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints in Zapopan, Jalisco, Mexico. The intent to build the temple was announced in a letter to local priesthood leaders on April 14, 1999, by the First Presidency.

text: Vicente Fox Quesada is a Mexican businessman and politician who served as the 62nd president of Mexico from 2000 to 2006. After campaigning as a right-wing populist, Fox was elected president on the National Action Party (PAN) ticket in the 2000 election.

title: The PAN win the gubernatorial election in Baja California, while the PRI regain the mayoralty of Chihuahua and make gains in Durango and Zacatecas.
text: A governor is an administrative leader and head of a polity or political region, in some cases, such as governors-general, as the head of a state's official representative. Depending on the type of political region or polity, a governor may be either appointed or elected, and the governor's powers can vary significantly, depending on the public laws in place locally.

title: Gay activist César Salazar Gongora is kidnapped and assaulted in Mérida, Yucatán, later facing threats for filing a complaint.
text: Gay is a term that primarily refers to a homosexual person or the trait of being homosexual. The term originally meant "carefree", "cheerful', or "bright and showy".

title: The 9/11 Terrorist attacks in the U.S. kill 31 Mexican citizens and prompt widespread sympathy in Mexico.
text: The September 11 attacks, colloquially known as 9/11, were a coordinated series of suicide attacks perpetrated by the Islamic terrorist organization al-Qaeda against the United States in 2001. A total of 19 hijackers commandeered four commercial passenger airliners.

title: Nuestra Belleza México 2001
text: Nuestra Belleza México 2001, the 8th Nuestra Belleza México pageant, was held at the Aeropuerto Internacional "Lic. Adolfo López Mateos" of Toluca, Estado de México, Mexico on September 28, 2001.

title: Human rights lawyer Digna Ochoa is found murdered in her Mexico City office; with a note left at the scene threatening her colleagues.
text: Digna Ochoa was a human rights lawyer in Mexico. During her career, Ochoa had represented some of Mexico's poorest constituents against government interests.

title: The Mexican Council on Foreign Relations is established
text: The Mexican Council on Foreign Relations was established the November 22, 2001. So far, it is the only plural and multidisciplinary forum, focused in the debate and analysis of Mexico's role in the world and the growing influence of international events on the national agenda.

title: Ernesto Fonseca Carrillo, convicted in the 1985 killing of DEA agent Enrique Camarena, is acquitted of drug trafficking charges but remains imprisoned.
text: Enrique Camarena Salazar was a Mexican-American agent of the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA). In February 1985, Camarena was kidnapped by police officers hired by the Guadalajara Cartel.

title: Primera División de México Verano 2001
text: Primera División de México Verano 2001 is a Mexican football tournament - one of two short tournaments that take up the entire year to determine the champion(s) of Mexican football. It began on Saturday, January 6, 2001, and ran until April 19, when the regular season ended.

title: Primera División de México Invierno 2001
text: Primera División de México Invierno 2001 is the second part of a two tournament season in Association football in Mexico. It began on July 21, 2001, and ended on November 25, the end of the season.

title: Mexico loses 2001 Copa América final to Colombia
text: The Mexico national football team represents Mexico in men's international football, and is governed by the Mexican Football Federation (Spanish: Federación Mexicana de Fútbol), the governing body for football in Mexico founded in 1927. It has been a full member of FIFA since 1929, is a founding member of CONCACAF which was founded in 1961, and is also a member of NAFU in the North American Zone.

title: 2001 Centrobasket is held in Toluca,
text: This page shows the results of the 2001 Men's Central American and Caribbean Basketball Championship, also known as the 2001 Centrobasket, which was held in the city of Toluca, Mexico from July 11 to July 15, 2001. The top four teams qualified for the 2001 Pan American Tournament, scheduled for August 16 to August 27 in Neuquén, Argentina.

title: Estudiantes de Altamira and Estudiantes de Xalapa are founded.
text: Altamira Fútbol Club or Estudiantes de Altamira was a Mexican football team based in Altamira, Tamaulipas.
